blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Managing tax obligations at the intermediate level means running a steady calendar rather than reacting to deadlines. Every tax has its own form, its own frequency, and its own risk if missed. VAT returns go out monthly or quarterly. Corporate tax goes out yearly, with a calendar full of smaller milestones along the way. Payroll taxes run every single pay cycle.

A calm tax team builds its calendar for the whole year, assigns owners, files returns early rather than late, and documents every position in case it is ever questioned. When a new rule arrives — as they always do — the team reads it, decides how it affects them, and updates the calendar.

Tax is rarely interesting. Done well, it is never dramatic either. Every quiet filing is a small victory that keeps the company off the regulator's radar — which is exactly where you want it to be.

items.q: According to the text, how often do VAT returns go out?
items.why: "VAT returns go out monthly or quarterly."

items.q: What does a calm tax team do with its returns?
options: Files them early rather than late
Waits until the deadline to file
items.why: "files returns early rather than late."

items.q: Why does the team document every position?
options: In case it is ever questioned later
items.why: "documents every position in case it is ever questioned."

items.q: The phrase "a small victory that keeps the company off the regulator's radar" suggests that…
options: Drawing regulatory attention is a sign of good work
Being noticed by the regulator is something to avoid
items.why: Inferência: ficar fora do radar é o objetivo — atenção do regulador é o que se quer evitar.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Every tax has its own frequency
New rules should trigger a calendar update
A single yearly calendar reduces last-minute panic
Good tax work should feel dramatic and exciting
items.why: Inferência: o texto valoriza o trabalho tranquilo e sem drama — "Done well, it is never dramatic either."

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte explicando como está montando o calendário fiscal da empresa. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me walk you through what I'm building. It's a single tax calendar for the whole company — every deadline, every owner, in one place. I don't want VAT sitting in one spreadsheet and payroll in another. If it's due, it's on this calendar.

For each entry, I've noted three things: what the tax is, how often it's filed, and who owns it. VAT is monthly, so it repeats twelve times. Corporate tax is once a year, but there are smaller milestones I've marked along the way so nothing surprises us in the final month.

Here's the part people usually skip. Next to every decision, I'm writing a short note — why we treated something the way we did. If a filing is ever questioned two years from now, we won't be guessing. We'll open the note and see exactly what we decided and why.

My rule is simple. We file early, never late. A quiet quarter with nothing dramatic is the best result we can get. If the regulator never has a reason to call, I've done my job.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Charlotte building?
options: A single tax calendar for the whole company
A separate spreadsheet for each tax
items.why: "a single tax calendar for the whole company — every deadline, every owner, in one place."

items.q: Which three things does Charlotte note for each entry?
options: The form, the fine, and the deadline
The amount, the bank, and the date
The country, the currency, and the client
The tax, how often it's filed, and who owns it
items.why: "what the tax is, how often it's filed, and who owns it."

items.q: Why does Charlotte write a short note next to every decision?
options: So the team won't be guessing if a filing is questioned later
To share it with the regulator immediately
items.why: "If a filing is ever questioned two years from now, we won't be guessing."

items.q: When Charlotte says "a quiet quarter with nothing dramatic is the best result," she implies that…
options: The absence of surprises is exactly what she is aiming for
Drama and problems are signs of a busy, successful team
items.why: Inferência: para ela, sucesso é a ausência de sustos, não o movimento.

items.q: How would you best describe Charlotte's approach?
options: Methodical and preventive — she plans and documents ahead
Reactive — she waits for deadlines to arrive
items.why: Inferência: um calendário único, notas e entregas antecipadas mostram um método preventivo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Each tax has its own frequency." Here, frequency means…
options: how often the tax must be filed
items.why: Frequency = frequência: com que periodicidade a declaração é entregue.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Corporate tax is annual, but there are smaller ___ along the way so nothing is left for the final month."
items.why: Milestone = marco: pontos intermediários ao longo do ano.

items.q: "Every VAT position is documented in case it is questioned." A position here is…
options: the stance taken on how a tax matter is treated
a job title in the tax team
a physical location in the office
items.why: Position = posição: a interpretação ou tratamento adotado sobre uma questão fiscal.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We ___ the return three days early so there was no last-minute rush."
items.why: To file = entregar/arquivar a declaração junto ao órgão competente.

items.q: "A quiet filing is a small victory." A quiet filing is one that…
options: is filed only at year end
is submitted without noise, problems, or regulator attention
is done in complete silence in the office
items.why: Quiet filing = entrega tranquila, sem sustos e sem chamar a atenção do regulador.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem no dia a dia de uma equipe fiscal. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The finance director still has to sign off on the annual return." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new tax calendar to every team next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two managers pushed back on the new filing schedule." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed to document every position but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "A new rule has arrived, so we need to keep on top of the changes." To keep on top of something means to…
options: stay fully in control and up to date with it
items.why: Keep on top of = manter-se por dentro e no controle de algo em movimento.
